sermon.title: Moses Like Jesus
sermon.speaker: Guest speaker (unnamed)
sermon.summary: Walking through Stephen’s sermon in Acts 7, this message shows how Moses was a prophet like Jesus: both fled a king, were rejected by their own, were sent by God to deliver, and did signs and wonders. The Red Sea pictures the torn veil, the golden calf pictures man-made religion, and God wants to dwell not in buildings but in us by his Spirit.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Delivered by a speaker other than Pastor Kincer (unnamed). He cites Acts 7:45 for David’s dwelling place (7:46–48) and lists “fire and brimstone” among the plagues (hail and fire). Sensitive content kept as spoken: beheadings with “Allahu Akbar,” the apostles all martyred except John.

chunks.section_question: Who was Stephen and why was he opposed?
chunks.short_answer: Stephen, full of grace and power, did great wonders while serving tables for widows. Religious opponents in Acts 6 could not stand against his wisdom or the Spirit by which he spoke, so they falsely accused him of blasphemy and brought him before the Sanhedrin, where he preached and was stoned.

faqs.question: Why read the Bible more than once?
faqs.answer: Each time you read it God can speak to you and open it up if you listen.

faqs.question: How does God change people?
faqs.answer: From the inside—Christ comes in and kills the sin and darkness.

faqs.question: Why did God use events in the Old Testament?
faqs.answer: To illustrate what he would do thousands of years later—something no man could do.

faqs.question: Is Jesus the only way?
faqs.answer: Yes—he is the door, and rejecting Christ is rejecting God.

faqs.question: How does the 400 years connect Moses and Christ?
faqs.answer: The speaker parallels 400 years of slavery in Egypt with 400 silent years before Christ came to free people from sin.

faqs.question: Who did the miracles through Moses?
faqs.answer: God did them; Moses was the vessel.

faqs.question: Is the Christian life always easy?
faqs.answer: No—there are dry seasons and wet seasons.

faqs.question: Does God need us?
faqs.answer: No—he doesn’t need anything, but he wants us and desires to live in us.

faqs.question: What takes a Christian to maturity?
